title: Hill Stations in Uttarakhand: Mussoorie, Nainital and the Kumaon Hills
seoTitle: Hill Stations in Uttarakhand: Mussoorie to Kumaon | Kudozz Club
metaDescription: Uttarakhand's hill stations compared: Mussoorie, Landour, Dhanaulti, Lansdowne, Nainital, Bhimtal, Ranikhet, Almora, Kausani, Mukteshwar, Munsiyari and Auli.
description: A guide to the hill stations of Uttarakhand: Mussoorie, Landour, Dhanaulti, Kanatal, Chakrata and Lansdowne in Garhwal; Nainital and its lakes, Ranikhet, Almora, Binsar, Kausani, Mukteshwar and Munsiyari in Kumaon; and Auli and Chopta in the high Garhwal, with seasons, access and how to combine them.
dek: Uttarakhand's hill stations are split between Garhwal and Kumaon, and between busy towns and quiet ridges with some of India's best Himalayan views.

hero.alt: Naini Lake seen from the hills above Nainital

intro: Uttarakhand has two hill regions. Garhwal, in the west, holds Mussoorie and Landour, Dhanaulti, Kanatal, Chakrata and Lansdowne, and further in, Auli and Chopta. Kumaon, in the east, has the lake town of Nainital and a chain of ridge towns (Ranikhet, Almora, Binsar, Kausani, Mukteshwar and Munsiyari) that look across to Nanda Devi, Trisul and Panchachuli.
Many of these towns are within a day of Delhi by road or train to Dehradun, Kathgodam or Kotdwar.
quickAnswer: The main hill stations in Uttarakhand are Mussoorie, Landour, Dhanaulti and Lansdowne in Garhwal, and Nainital, Bhimtal, Ranikhet, Almora, Kausani, Mukteshwar and Munsiyari in Kumaon; Auli is the ski slope near Joshimath. March to June and October to December are the best months, with the clearest Himalayan views from October to December. Avoid long drives in the monsoon, when landslides are common.
takeaways: Mussoorie and Nainital are the classic, busy hill towns; Kumaon's ridges are quieter.
Kausani, Binsar, Mukteshwar and Munsiyari have outstanding views of the high Himalaya in clear weather.
Auli is India's best-known ski slope outside Kashmir; the Joshimath-Auli ropeway has not operated since 2023.
Railheads are Dehradun (Garhwal), Kathgodam (Kumaon) and Kotdwar (Lansdowne).
The monsoon brings landslides; October to December is the clearest period.

sections.heading: Getting there
list: Dehradun (Jolly Grant airport and railway) for Mussoorie, Dhanaulti and Chakrata.
Kathgodam railway station and Pantnagar airport for Nainital and the Kumaon towns.
Haridwar and Rishikesh for the drive up to Auli and Chopta.

sections.heading: A little history
paras: Mussoorie and Landour were developed from the 1820s as a hill retreat and cantonment above Dehradun, and Nainital was founded as a settlement in 1841 and later became the summer capital of the United Provinces. Ranikhet and Lansdowne grew as cantonments. Almora is much older, a seat of the Chand kings of Kumaon, and the region's temples, such as Jageshwar, go back more than a thousand years.

sections.heading: Where to stay
paras: In Mussoorie, Landour and the Camel's Back Road area are quieter than the Mall Road end. In Nainital, the Mall is lively but congested; Bhimtal and Sattal are calmer lake alternatives. The Kumaon ridges have small resorts, homestays and heritage bungalows with views; in winter, confirm heating and whether the road to your stay stays open after snow.

sections.heading: Good combinations
list: Rishikesh and Mussoorie, with Dhanaulti for a quiet night.
Nainital with Mukteshwar and Kausani on a Kumaon loop.
Lansdowne as a two-night break from Delhi.
Rishikesh with Chopta and Tungnath for a short trek.

sections.heading: When to go
list: March to June: pleasant; Mussoorie and Nainital are very busy in May and June.
July to September: heavy rain and landslides; keep drives short and flexible.
October to December: crisp, clear and the best time for mountain views.
January to February: cold; snow is likely at Auli and possible at Mussoorie, Dhanaulti, Nainital and Mukteshwar.

safety: Mountain roads close or slow down after heavy rain, snow or landslides; check road and weather updates, and avoid driving after dark.
Permits, e-passes, ropeways and pass openings change; check official portals before you travel.
Carry warm layers even in summer; nights in the hills are cool.
packing: Warm layers and a waterproof jacket

faqs.q: Which is the best hill station in Uttarakhand?
faqs.a: Mussoorie and Nainital are the most popular; Kausani, Mukteshwar and Lansdowne are quieter.

faqs.q: Which Uttarakhand hill station is closest to Delhi?
faqs.a: Lansdowne, Mussoorie and Nainital are each roughly 250 to 320 km by road.
The Joshimath-Auli ropeway has not operated since the 2023 Joshimath land-subsidence crisis; check locally before planning around it.

faqs.q: Where can I see the high Himalaya from Uttarakhand?
faqs.a: Kausani, Binsar, Mukteshwar, Munsiyari and Chopta in clear weather.

faqs.q: When is the best time to visit?
faqs.a: March to June and October to December.
